sentences.text: Sri Bhagwan vs Jai Singh on 12 October, 2023

Bench: Hrishikesh Roy, Pankaj Mithal
 1
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Civil Appellate Jurisdiction
CIVIL APPEAL Nos.9624-9626 OF 2010  SRI BHAGWAN   VERSUS  JAI SINGH   O R D E R Heard Mr. Harsh Aggarwal, learned counsel appearing for the appellant.
The respondent is one of the plaintiffs in the Suit No.751 of 1988 and is represented by Mr. Mandeep Singh Vinaik, learned counsel.
2. The suit was filed for a decree of specific performance in relation to the agreement dated 07.12.1987.
The agreement was executed by the appellant- Sri Bhagwan along with his two siblings and the purchasers were Jai Singh and his two brothers, Sher Singh and Inder Singh.

As a part performance of the agreement, the buyers advanced Rs.60,000/- paid in two tranche (Rs.50,000/-
and then Rs.10,000/-) and the total sale consideration was determined at Rs.30/- per square yard for the land measuring 26 kanals and 17 Marlas located at village Jhar-Saintly, Tehsil Ballabhgarh,
District Faridabad.

3. The learned Additional Civil Judge (Sr. Division), Faridabad decreed the suit on 28.01.1997 in favour of the plaintiffs by saying that in terms of the agreement dated 07.12.1987 the defendants are required to execute the sale deed of land measuring 26 kanals and 17 marlas on payment of the balance sale consideration of Rs.4,27,290/- in favour of the defendants.
On execution of the sale deed, the three plaintiffs together were held entitled to get joint possession of the land.
4. The aggrieved defendants then moved to the Appellate Court in the Civil Appeal No.33 of 1997.
While the appeal was pending, the suit land was subjected to acquisition by the authorities.

The plaintiffs accordingly sought amendment of the plaint in terms of the Section 21(5) of the Specific Relief Act 1963 and the amendment prayer was granted by the Court on 26.03.1999.
5.
The learned District Judge, Faridabad assessed the merit of the defendants challenge and dismissed the Civil Appeal No.33 of 1997 filed by the appellant.

In the altered circumstances of the land being acquired and the consequential amendment of the plaint, the Appellate Court held that the plaintiffs shall be entitled for the awarded compensation from the Collector but the plaintiffs shall also pay the balance amount of Rs.4,27,290/- to the defendants.

1 6.

The aggrieved defendants then filed the RSA No.3170 of 1999 before the Punjab and Haryana High Court at Chandigarh but the High Court under the impugned order dated 02.09.2008 upheld the concurrent decree in favour of the plaintiffs and dismissed the defendants second appeal.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 7. It may be mentioned at this stage that when the second appeal was pending before the High Court, on 18.05.2004 a compromise was allegedly reached between the defendants on the one side and two of the plaintiffs  Sher Singh and Inder Singh on the other side.
But since the said compromise was not supported by Jai Singh (Plaintiff No.1), he moved Court to say that no compromise was reached between the plaintiffs and the defendants.

8. In any case, the case filed by the defendants in the High Court was contested only by Jai Singh (plaintiff No.1) and the High Court noted that the defendants have suffered decree for specific performance in two courts and assessing the legal position endorsed the view that the defendants have committed breach of the sale agreement.

However, because of the acquisition of the land,
which was the subject matter of the sale agreement, the Court opined that decree of specific performance is not capable of execution and therefore the acquisition compensation was rightly held to be payable to the plaintiffs, by the Appellate Court.

As the contesting plaintiff was one amongst the three brothers, the appeal came to be dismissed with the following direction of the High Court:-
The appellants shall pay 1/3rd of the amount of compensation received by them from the Land Acquisition Collector including interest, if any, received, to the contesting respondents (legal representatives of plaintiff No.3, deceased Inder Singh), within a period of two months, failing which the respondents shall be entitled to interest at the rate of 4% per annum from the expiry of period of two months till the amount is actually paid.
The respondents are also entitled to execute the decree on failure of the appellants to pay the compensation within time specified herein-above.

9. The submission of the learned counsel for the appellant is that the decree of specific performance is an equitable relief and the Court having regard to Clause 7 and Clause 10 of the sale agreement,
should not have ordered for the relief of specific performance of the sale agreement.

The Appellants counsel would rely on Kanshi Ram Vs. Omprakash Jawal & Ors1 to argue that granting decree of specific performance of a contract of immovable 1 . AIR 1996 SC 2150 property is not automatic and relief is to be granted in exercise of equitable discretion.

entities.text: Kanshi Ram Vs. Omprakash Jawal & Ors1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10. Representing the respondent-plaintiff, Mr. Mandeep Singh Vinaik, the learned counsel would however argue that since the plaintiffs got their plaint amended to incorporate the prayer relatable to Section 21(5) of the Specific Performance Act and amendment having been allowed without contest by the other side, the direction issued by the Appellant Court moulding the relief for the plaintiffs to receive the compensation amount from the Collector, should brook no interference from this Court.

In fairness, the counsel would submit that since the plaintiff No.2 and plaintiff No.3 are not contesting the proceeding, the relief to the extent of 1/3rd of the compensation amount was rightly granted by the High Court for the sole contesting plaintiff.

2 11. Section 21 of the Specific Relief Act empowers the Court to award compensation in a suit for specific performance of a contract in the event of any breach in the performance of such contract, by the defendant.
Unless the plaintiff claims compensation in his plaint, compensation is not awardable under sub-Section (5) of Section 21 of the Act.

Sub-Section (4) provides for the determination of the amount of compensation awarded under Section 21 and it is specified that the Court shall be guided by the principles specified in Section 73 of the Indian Contract Act 1973.
12.
The consequences of breach of contract are mentioned in Chapter VI of the Contract Act.
Section 73 provides for compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of the contract.

13. The aforenoted statutory provisions indicate that compensation can be awarded either for the actual damage caused naturally in the breach of contract or to the extent of suffering by a party on account of the breach committed by the other party.

14. The learned Judge in the impugned judgment took note of Clause 10 of the sale agreement dated 07.12.1987 which provided that the plaintiff is also entitled to recover from the vendor the amount paid as earnest money along with interest and they shall also be entitled to receive damage quantified at Rs.1,00,000/-.
Clause 7 of the sale agreement deals with a situation when the land is subjected to acquisition by the Government or any other authority.
In such circumstances, the parties have agreed that the vendee alone shall be entitled to entire compensation amount that is assessed by the authorities.

15. While dealing with the inter-play between the provisions of Section 21(2), (4) and (5) and Section 73 of the Contract Act in a suit for specific performance of contract for purchase of land in Jagdish vs. Natthu Singh2, Justice M.N. Venkatachaliah on behalf of the Bench made the following pertinent observation:-
27. The measure of the compensation is by the standards of Section 73 of the Indian Contract Act.

Here again the English rule in Bain v. Fothergill [(1874) LR 7 HL 158 :
31 LT 387] that the purchaser, on breach of the contract, cannot recover for the loss of his bargain is not applicable.

entities.text:
Bain v. Fothergill [(1874) LR 7 HL 158 :
31 LT 387]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In Pollock & Mulla on Contract (10th edn.) the law on the matter is set out thus: (p.
663)

Where, therefore, a purchaser of land claims damages for the loss of his bargain, the question to be decided is whether the damages alleged to have been caused to him naturally arose in the usual course of things from such breach; and in an ordinary case it would be difficult to hold otherwise.
In the present case there is no difficulty in assessing the quantum of the compensation.
That is ascertainable with reference to the determination of the market value in the land acquisition proceedings.

The compensation awarded may safely be taken to be the measure of damages subject, of course, to the deduction therefrom of money value of the services, time and energy expended by the appellant in pursuing the claims of compensation and the expenditure incurred by him in the Sri Bhagwan vs Jai Singh on 12 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120073476/
3 litigation culminating in the award 16.
The above ratio in Jagdish Singh (supra) was followed subsequently in Urmila Devi and Others vs. Deity, Mandir Shree Chamunda Devi Through Temple Commissioner and Others3 and Sukhbir vs. Ajit Singh4.

entities.text: Urmila Devi and Others vs. Deity, Mandir Shree Chamunda Devi Through Temple Commissioner and Others3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In Sukhbir (supra), the Court endorsing the ratio in Jagdish Singh (supra) and Urmila Devi (supra) noted the following:-
12.

Now so far as the amount of compensation is concerned, as observed by this Court in Jagdish Singh [Jagdish Singh v. Natthu Singh, (1992) 1 SCC 647] , the compensation determined and awarded under the Land Acquisition Act may safely be taken into consideration.

entities.text: Jagdish Singh [Jagdish Singh v. Natthu Singh, (1992) 1 SCC 647]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the High Court has rightly observed and held that the plaintiff shall be entitled to the entire amount of compensation awarded under the Land Acquisition Act together with interest and solatium.

However, at the same time, the defendant, original landowner shall also be entitled to the deduction therefrom of money value of the services, time and energy expended in pursuing the claims of compensation and the expenditure incurred by him in the litigation culminating in the award.
As such, nothing is on record to suggest that any expenses have been incurred by the appellant.

However, in the facts and circumstances of the case and considering the decisions of this Court in Jagdish Singh [Jagdish Singh v. Natthu Singh, (1992) 1 SCC 647] and Urmila Devi [Urmila Devi v.
Mandir Shree Chamunda Devi, (2018) 2 SCC 284 :
(2018) 1 SCC (Civ) 558] , ends of justice will be served if the plaintiff is awarded the entire amount of compensation determined under the Land Acquisition Act together with interest and solatium less Rs 2,50,000 + Rs 50,000 (towards the balance sale consideration).
17.

sentences.text: Being guided by the above ratio in Jagdish Singh (supra), Urmila Devi (supra) and Sukhbir (supra), the only way to understand 3 .

(2021) 6 SCC 54 the judgments under challenge is that after the plaint was amended to incorporate the prayers under Section 21(5) of the Specific Relief Act, the Court had granted the alternate relief of awarding the compensation amount in favour of the plaintiff.
Thus, a fair and equitable decree was granted under the altered circumstances, following the acquisition of the subject land.
18. It must also be borne in mind that the defendants challenge concurrent decree of three Courts and we see no reason to disturb such finding in favour of plaintiff.
19. In consequence, the decree-holder (plaintiff No.1) is held entitled to 1/3rd of the compensation sum along with any interest accruing to the said amount.
However, this is subject to adjustment of the amount already received by the plaintiff No.1.

Since execution proceedings are pending,
following the decree to the extent of 1/3rd of the compensation amount in favour of plaintiff No.1,
the Executing Court will take necessary steps for disbursal of the due sum to the decree-holder.

It is,
however, made clear that the plaintiff No.1 after receipt of the 1/3 rd of the acquisition money must Sri Bhagwan vs Jai Singh on 12 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120073476/
4 remit his 1/3rd liability of Rs.4,27,290/-, due to the appellant-defendant.
20. With the above order, the appeals stand dismissed, leaving the parties to bear their own cost.
